values.spoken: up to six times the throughput of MySQL

values.display: up to 6x the throughput of stock PostgreSQL
values.spoken: up to six times the throughput of PostgreSQL

evidence.quote: Aurora delivers up to 6x the throughput of stock PostgreSQL and up to 6x the throughput of stock MySQL on similar hardware.
Testing on standard benchmarks such as SysBench has shown an increase in throughput of up to 6x over stock PostgreSQL and stock MySQL on similar hardware.

note: d27-002. The Aurora User Guide, FAQ and features page all say 6x; the expected 5x and 3x figures are not in those pages.

claim: You can achieve read scaling by creating up to 15 Aurora Replicas in a DB cluster. Each Aurora Replica returns the same data from the cluster volume with minimal replica lag, usually considerably less than 100 milliseconds after the primary instance has written an update.
question: How many Aurora Replicas can you create for read scaling, and what lag does the User Guide state?

evidence.quote: You can achieve read scaling for your Aurora DB cluster by creating up to 15 Aurora Replicas in a DB cluster. Each Aurora Replica returns the same data from the cluster volume with minimal replica lag—usually considerably less than 100 milliseconds after the primary instance has written an update.

claim: Aurora Replicas do not have to be of the same DB instance class as the primary instance, although AWS recommends the same class for high-availability replicas.
question: Must an Aurora Replica use the same DB instance class as the primary instance?

values.display: don't have to be of the same DB instance class as the primary instance

evidence.quote: Aurora Replicas don't have to be of the same DB instance class as the primary instance.
These should be of the same DB instance class as the primary instance and in different Availability Zones for your Aurora DB cluster.
